title: Coordinated Execution: Benchmarks & Sampling Protocol
author: Aisha Gupta
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines a coordinated execution benchmark and sampling protocol for validating scheduler and kernel interactions across mixed inference workloads. It complements existing per-component tests by providing a reproducible end-to-end measurement harness, standardized metrics, and a lightweight on-call triage flow for anomalies that arise during benchmark runs.

Goals
-----
- Provide an experiment protocol that produces stable, comparable signals for: latency P50/P95/P99, token throughput, per-token GPU time, kernel-switch rate, and KV-cache hit/miss impact.
- Standardize sampling, tracing, and aggregation so regression hunts can compare like-for-like across runtime versions and hardware shapes.
- Offer step-by-step runbook sections for running, interpreting, and responding to benchmark anomalies.

Scope and Non-Goals
-------------------
- Scope: multi-tenant mixed inference profiles (chat + single-turn generation + long-context summarization), scheduler interaction patterns (admission, preemption, handoff), and sampling-based profiling to attribute tail latency to kernel or network layers.
- Non-goals: this is not a replacement for microbenchmarks (kernel unit tests) nor for customer-specific capacity planning; it should be used as a cross-cutting integration verification and regression detector.

Overview of the Protocol
------------------------
1. Define workload cohorts: head (short chat, 8–64 tokens), mid (generation, 64–512 tokens), tail (long-context, 512–4k tokens). Each cohort has an associated QPS target and entropy profile.
2. Synthesize request surface: use the workload corpus generator (see Appendix) to produce deterministic request sequences for each cohort.
3. Run a staged experiment matrix across hardware shapes and kernel build variants. For each cell collect: end-to-end traces (sampled), kernel-level traces (per-dispatch timestamps), and telemetry counters (scheduler signals, admission events, eviction events).
4. Apply the sampling and aggregation rules below to produce a canonical report.

Workload Cohort Definitions
- Head: 100ms target latency, 8–64 tokens, QPS per-cohort: 100–300.
- Mid: 200–500ms target, 64–512 tokens, QPS: 10–50.
- Tail: 500ms–5s target, 512–4k tokens, QPS: 0.5–5.

Key Metrics (aggregation rules)
- Latency: P50/P90/P95/P99 measured end-to-end and kernel-only. Kernel-only = sum(kernel execution windows on device).
- Token throughput: tokens/sec measured per-cohort and aggregated weighted by customer-weighted token shares.
- Kernel-switch rate: number of kernel handoffs per request (normalize by sequence length).
- KV-cache hit ratio and miss latency contribution: report absolute and delta vs baseline.
- Preemption/eviction rate: events per 1k requests.

Sampling & Tracing Rules
------------------------
- Deterministic seed: All synthetic corpora must be generated with a fixed RNG seed per experiment id. Record the seed in the run metadata.
- Stratified sampling: sample 1 in N end-to-end requests per cohort to capture full trace data. N is chosen so that overhead < 2% CPU and <1% GPU time: default N=100 for head, 50 for mid, 10 for tail.
- Kernel-level sampling: enable fine-grained kernel timestamps for 1 in 500 kernel invocations (circular buffer). These traces should be uploaded as compressed artifacts for offline attribution.
- Trace metadata requirements: every trace must include request id, cohort tag, sequence length, model variant id, kernel-variant tag, scheduler-policy snapshot, and node/hardware id.

Telemetry Signals to Collect
- Scheduler: admission decisions, slot allocation, priority buckets, preemption timestamp, backpressure signals.
- Kernel: kernel_id, kernel_variant, start_ts, end_ts, device_mem_used, thread_block_count.
- Network / RPC: inbound queue time, serialization time, outbound flush latency.
- KV-cache: shard_id, hit/miss, fetch_latency, warmup_state.

Experiment Matrix Example (table)
| Dimension          | Values / Notes                      | Default selection |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------|-------------------|
| Hardware shape    | A100x8, A100x4, L40x8, H100x8        | A100x8            |
| Model variant     | fp16, int8-quant, trimmed-ctx       | fp16              |
| Scheduler policy  | latency-first, economic-governor    | latency-first     |
| Load pattern      | steady, poisson-burst, diurnal-saw  | steady            |
| Cohort mix        | 70/25/5 head/mid/tail               | 70/25/5           |

Pass/Fail Criteria (example thresholds)
- Kernel P99 regression: fail if kernel-only P99 increases > 15% vs baseline.
- End-to-end P99: fail if > 25% increase OR absolute > 2s for mid cohort.
- KV-cache miss contribution: fail if miss-induced latency increases > 30ms average.

Investigation & Triage Runbook
------------------------------
1. Validate inputs: confirm RNG seed, cohort mix, and hardware cell match the experiment matrix.
2. Compare traces: aggregate top-3 root cause candidates by per-request kernel-only latency contribution.
3. Check scheduler signals: are admission delays or preemptions elevated? Check admission queue length and priority inversion counters.
4. Inspect kernel histogram: look for new long-tail modes indicating kernel stalls or thermal throttling.
5. Inspect device metrics: GPU SM utilization, PCIe transfer spikes, and nvlink error counters.
6. If kernel-only latency is unchanged but end-to-end regresses, inspect RPC and serialization metrics and network egress congestion.
7. Run targeted microbenchmarks: isolate suspect kernel variant on controlled single-tenant run to confirm reproducer.
8. If reproducer found, create an issue with: run id, seed, failing metrics, top traces (compressed), and suggested hypothesis.

Quick Mitigations (operational)
- Swap scheduler policy to economic-governor for degraded tail pressure scenarios.
- Pin cohort-heavy customers to isolation pool (dedicated capacity) if noisy neighbor observed.
- Temporarily enable kernel hedging for long tail requests (config toggle, see Runtime Flags table).

Runtime Flags & Configuration Table
| Flag name                         | Purpose                                      | Recommended value |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| runtime.benchmark.sample_rate    | stratified sampling divisor (per-cohort)     | head:100,mid:50,tail:10 |
| runtime.kernel.trace_window      | kernel-level trace buffer (entries)          | 500               |
| runtime.scheduler.policy         | active scheduler profile                     | latency-first     |
| runtime.kv.prefetch_threshold    | tokens ahead to prefetch                     | 64                |

Release Checklist (when using this protocol for a CVE/regression gate)
- Update canonical baseline artifact (store in artifact repo with run id).
- Run full experiment matrix across two hardware shapes.
- Ensure telemetry upload succeeded and artifacts are checksumed.
- Attach report + top 10 worst traces to PR and tag on-call owners.

Ownership and Contact
---------------------
- Owner: serving-runtime benchmarking team (oncall alias: eng-runtime-bench@redwood.example.com).
- Escalation: if evidence of hardware degradation, escalate to eng-infra GPU fleet team (pager: eng-gpu-fleet).

Appendix A — Example benchmark config (YAML)
```
experiment_id: coordinated-exec-2026-02
seed: 452318
cohort_mix:
  head: 70
  mid: 25
  tail: 5
hardware: A100x8
scheduler_policy: latency-first
sampling:
  head: 1/100
  mid: 1/50
  tail: 1/10
tracing:
  kernel_sample_divisor: 500
  artifacts_retention_days: 14
```

Appendix B — CLI snippets
- Start a run: redwood-bench run --config path/to/config.yaml --out /tmp/run-artifacts --note "perf-tuning-experiment"
- Upload artifacts: redwood-bench upload /tmp/run-artifacts --repo experiments/coord-exec
- Create quick report: redwood-bench report /tmp/run-artifacts --format html > /tmp/report.html

Appendix C — Example failure report template
- Run id: <run id>
- Baseline id: <baseline id>
- Delta metrics: {end_to_end_p99: +X%, kernel_only_p99: +Y%} 
- Top 5 traces (compressed path): /artifacts/<run>/trace-1.gz ...
- Hypothesis: <short description>
- Next steps: <list>
